sources.label: ADR-001: store UTC, render and schedule in the stop's zone
sources.excerpt: Decision: 1. Every instant persisted by the service is a UTC ISO-8601 string of the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ. 2. Each itinerary stop carries the IANA zone of the place (stop.timezone), validated on write. 3. Anything user-facing that is about a stop — displayed times, "morning of" computations, reminders scheduled relative to the stop — is computed in stop.timezone. The traveller's homeTimezone is for account-level display only and must not be used to derive stop-relative instants. 4. All zone math goes through src/itinerary/timezone.ts (toZoned, fromZoned, atLocalTime, formatInZone). Consequences: Reviewers should treat a homeTimezone reference outside trips/ as a smell and ask for the stop's zone instead.

sources.label: ADR-002: money in minor units; FX locked at quote time
sources.excerpt: Decision: money is { amountMinor: integer, currency: ISO-4217 }. A quote captures fxRate and quotedAt once; bookings and displays reuse the quoted amount and never re-apply a rate. src/pricing/money.ts and src/pricing/quote.ts implement this.

sources.label: ADR-003: client-generated bookingRef is the provider idempotency key
sources.excerpt: Decision: the client generates bookingRef before the first provider call. Every attempt, including retries in src/providers/retry.ts (max 3, jittered backoff), forwards the same bookingRef as the provider's idempotency key; adapters must treat a repeated ref as the same reservation. Never mint a new request id per attempt.

sources.label: ADR-004: provider search results cached 10 minutes, keyed by currency too
sources.excerpt: Decision: search responses are cached for 10 minutes in src/providers/cache.ts under (origin, destination, date, currency). Currency is part of the key because provider quotes are currency-specific and must not be reconverted.

sources.label: ADR-005: itinerary stops are soft-deleted
sources.excerpt: Decision: deleting a stop sets deletedAt instead of removing the row so bookings keep their history. Consequence: anything scheduled against a stop (reminders in src/notifications) must treat a stop with deletedAt as cancelled and must not fire.

sources.label: CONTRIBUTING.md reviewer checklist
sources.excerpt: Reviewer checklist: instants stored UTC and rendered in the stop's zone; money in minor units with the quoted FX; bookingRef forwarded on every provider attempt; search cache key includes currency; soft-deleted stops cancel their reminders. Trips have exactly one traveller; providers are in-process fakes with injected latency and timeouts so tests are deterministic.

sources.label: PR #2: itinerary stops with IANA zones (ADR-001)
sources.excerpt: Follow-ups: Reminders/notifications will consume atLocalTime for "morning of the stop" nudges. Whoever picks that up: use the stop's zone, per the ADR. Soft deletion of stops is not in scope here; stops are append-only for now. — Seed adds a Tokyo and a Lisbon stop to the New York traveller's trip so the demo data spans three zones.

sources.label: Pull request: trip reminders
sources.excerpt: Adds src/notifications/reminders.ts and scheduler.ts. Reminder instants are computed from the traveller's home zone for now; tests/reminders.test.ts has a skipped case for a stop in another zone with a TODO to switch to the stop's zone.

sources.label: Pull request: provider adapters, retry, cache
sources.excerpt: Adds flights/hotels adapters with retry and cache. Known gap: the hotel adapter builds a fresh provider request id on each retry attempt instead of forwarding bookingRef; a skipped test in tests/hotels.test.ts documents the duplicate reservation after a timeout.

claims.title: Instants are stored as UTC; user-facing times use the stop's IANA zone
claims.content: All instants are persisted as UTC ISO-8601 strings. Any time shown to a traveller or used to schedule something on their behalf must be computed in the time zone of the itinerary stop it belongs to (stop.timezone, an IANA zone such as Asia/Tokyo), never in the traveller's home zone (trip.homeTimezone), which is for account-level display only. All zone math goes through src/itinerary/timezone.ts: atLocalTime(instant, stop.timezone, hour, minute) gives '08:00 on the stop's local day' as a UTC instant; toZoned/fromZoned convert; formatInZone displays. No other module may call Intl.DateTimeFormat with a timeZone or do offset arithmetic. A homeTimezone reference outside src/trips/ is a review smell.
claims.summary: Store UTC; render and schedule in stop.timezone via atLocalTime/toZoned in src/itinerary/timezone.ts, never trip.homeTimezone.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-001 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: ADR-001: store UTC, render and schedule in the stop's zone
claims.content: Context: a trip spans several places with their own clocks; trip.homeTimezone arrived first with the trips scaffold and is the tempting, wrong default for anything about a stop. Decision: persist UTC ISO strings (offset input normalised, offset-less input rejected as ambiguous); each stop carries a validated IANA zone; everything about a stop is computed in stop.timezone; all zone math lives in src/itinerary/timezone.ts. Consequences: instants sort lexicographically; DST is handled in one place (spring-forward gaps shift forward, fall-back overlaps take the earlier offset); any feature computing a time 'for the traveller' must ask which place it is about — in particular the reminders module in src/notifications/.
claims.summary: Why every displayed or scheduled time takes the stop's zone as input.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-001 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: Trip reminders are scheduled in the traveller's home zone instead of the stop's zone
claims.content: src/notifications/reminders.ts computes the reminder instant with trip.homeTimezone. For a stop whose zone differs from the traveller's home zone the reminder fires at the wrong local time (the seed data has a New York traveller with Tokyo and Lisbon stops: a 'morning of' Tokyo reminder fires at New York morning). The fix is to derive the instant from stop.timezone with atLocalTime(stop.startsAt, stop.timezone, hour) from src/itinerary/timezone.ts, per ADR-001. tests/reminders.test.ts contains the skipped reproduction.
claims.summary: reminders.ts uses trip.homeTimezone; should use atLocalTime(…, stop.timezone, …) from src/itinerary/timezone.ts.
claims.changeReason: Known issue recorded from the trip reminders pull request

claims.title: A soft-deleted stop cancels everything scheduled against it
claims.content: Itinerary stops are never hard-deleted; deletion sets stop.deletedAt. Any scheduled work keyed to a stop — reminders in src/notifications/scheduler.ts in particular — must check deletedAt at fire time and skip (cancel) rather than send. Queries that list active stops must filter deletedAt IS NULL.
claims.summary: Check stop.deletedAt before firing; soft-deleted stops must not notify.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-005 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: ADR-005: soft-delete itinerary stops
claims.content: Context: bookings reference stops and travellers expect to see what they cancelled. Decision: deleting a stop sets deletedAt; rows stay. Consequence: every consumer of stops (notifications, pricing summaries) must respect deletedAt, and the scheduler treats a deleted stop as a cancelled reminder.
claims.summary: Stops keep their rows; consumers filter on deletedAt.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-005 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: Money is integer minor units with a currency; FX is locked at quote time
claims.content: Amounts are { amountMinor: integer, currency }. Never use floating-point currency values. A quote captures fxRate and quotedAt exactly once in src/pricing/quote.ts; bookings copy the quoted amount and displays format it. Re-applying an FX rate at booking or display time is a defect.
claims.summary: Integer minor units; the quote's fxRate is the only conversion.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-002 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: ADR-002: minor units and FX locked at quote time
claims.content: Context: floating-point totals drifted and re-converted prices changed between search and checkout. Decision: integer minor units everywhere; a single fxRate captured on the quote. Consequence: src/pricing/money.ts is the only arithmetic helper; bookings never convert.
claims.summary: Why prices are frozen on the quote.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-002 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: Every provider attempt forwards the same client bookingRef as the idempotency key
claims.content: The client generates bookingRef before the first provider call. src/providers/retry.ts retries failed or timed-out calls up to 3 times with jittered backoff and must pass the identical bookingRef on each attempt; adapters send it as the provider idempotency key and treat a repeated ref as the same reservation. Minting a new request id per attempt can create duplicate reservations after a timeout.
claims.summary: Retries reuse bookingRef; adapters must not generate per-attempt ids.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-003 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: ADR-003: client-generated bookingRef as provider idempotency key
claims.content: Context: provider timeouts are common with the fake providers' injected latency and would be with real ones. Decision: idempotency is owned by the caller, not the adapter, so retries are safe by construction. Consequence: src/bookings/idempotency.ts generates and persists the ref; adapters forward it unchanged.
claims.summary: Why idempotency lives with the caller.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-003 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: Hotel adapter mints a new request id per retry, duplicating reservations after a timeout
claims.content: src/providers/hotels.ts builds a fresh provider request id inside each attempt instead of forwarding the caller's bookingRef. When the first attempt times out but succeeds provider-side, the retry creates a second reservation. tests/hotels.test.ts holds the skipped reproduction. The fix is to pass bookingRef through unchanged as the idempotency key, matching src/providers/flights.ts.
claims.summary: hotels.ts ignores bookingRef on retries; should forward it like flights.ts.
claims.changeReason: Known issue recorded from the provider adapters pull request

claims.title: Provider search cache is keyed by origin, destination, date, and currency for 10 minutes
claims.content: src/providers/cache.ts caches search results for 10 minutes under (origin, destination, date, currency). Currency is part of the key because provider quotes are currency-specific and must not be reconverted (see the money constraint). Omitting currency from the key serves one traveller another traveller's currency.
claims.summary: Cache key must include currency; TTL 10 minutes.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-004 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: ADR-004: cache provider search results
claims.content: Context: repeated searches hit provider rate limits. Decision: a 10-minute in-memory cache in src/providers/cache.ts keyed by route, date, and currency; rateLimit.ts stays as the backstop. Consequence: quote.ts reads through the cache and must pass the traveller's currency.
claims.summary: Why search goes through a currency-aware cache.
claims.changeReason: Curated from ADR-004 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: A trip has exactly one traveller
claims.content: Trips carry one traveller with one home zone and one currency; group trips are out of scope. Code that needs 'the traveller' can read it from the trip without ambiguity.
claims.summary: No group trips; trip.traveller is singular.
claims.changeReason: Curated from CONTRIBUTING.md for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: Providers are in-process fakes with injected latency and timeouts
claims.content: src/providers/fake/* implement the flight and hotel provider interfaces without network access. Latency and timeouts are injected per call so retry and idempotency behaviour is deterministic under test. No provider credentials exist anywhere in the project.
claims.changeReason: Curated from CONTRIBUTING.md for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: Each stop stores its own validated IANA zone; the traveller's zone is account-level only
claims.content: stop.timezone is written and validated (isValidTimeZone/assertTimeZone) when the stop is created, and stop responses include a display block already rendered in that zone so clients never convert. Consumers must read the stored zone rather than infer one from the destination or from trip.homeTimezone, which exists only for the account-level 'your trips' view.
claims.summary: Read stop.timezone; never infer a zone from the destination or the traveller.
claims.changeReason: Curated from PR #2 for the Tripline demo project

claims.title: The scheduler tick compares UTC instants; zone only matters when choosing the wall-clock target
claims.content: src/notifications/scheduler.ts polls due reminders by comparing stored UTC instants with now(). Zone handling therefore belongs where the target instant is computed (reminders.ts), not in the scheduler loop.
claims.summary: Fix zone bugs where the instant is computed, not in the scheduler.
claims.changeReason: Recorded from the trip reminders pull request
